decisions.decision: Version forecasting inputs in a data version repository
decisions.context: Forecasts must be reproducible for any past week, so each run needs a traceable snapshot of its input data. The design space offers a dedicated data version repository, code repository versioning, or no data versioning (d:11).
decisions.rationale: A data version repository directly supports repeatable forecasts by preserving the inputs used for each run (d:11, v:11.1). The checked point had no warnings; it was unattested, while the rival point without versioning was also unattested.
consequences: Record the input data version with each forecast run.
Maintain the repository and its retention policy.

decisions.decision: Process weekly demand data in batches
decisions.context: The brief specifies weekly forecasts per store and product, with no real-time requirement. Batch processing fits the stated cadence (d:15).
decisions.rationale: Weekly batch processing matches the brief’s forecast cadence and avoids introducing streaming operations without a stated need (d:15, v:15.1). The checked point had no warnings; it was unattested, as was the streaming rival.
consequences: Forecasts refresh on the weekly schedule.
Late-arriving data needs an explicit rerun policy.

decisions.context: The production forecast must run weekly, which maps directly to a scheduled pipeline trigger (d:12).

alternatives.label: On-commit trigger
pros: Runs after code or data changes
cons: Does not itself enforce weekly cadence

decisions.rationale: A schedule makes the required weekly execution predictable; ad hoc and commit triggers can supplement it for reruns or changed inputs (d:12, v:12.3).
consequences: Track completion and alert on missed runs.
Provide a controlled rerun path for corrected inputs.

decisions.decision: Use a CI/CD pipeline for model and system releases
decisions.context: New model ideas should reach production quickly, while weekly runs must remain stable. Automated integration and delivery provides a repeatable release path (d:8).
decisions.rationale: CI/CD automates the release path and supports rapid model updates with repeatable checks (d:8, v:8.1). The checked design point had no warnings, but its combination was unattested; a rival with manual deployment scripts and no automation was also unattested.
consequences: Maintain automated build and release definitions.
Keep weekly forecasting runs independent of code commits.

decisions.decision: Train forecasting models with batch learning
decisions.context: The brief describes weekly forecasts and reproducibility for past weeks, with no requirement for online updates. Batch learning aligns training with versioned historical inputs (d:19).

alternatives.label: Hybrid batch-based and incremental learning
cons: Harder to operate with a small team

decisions.rationale: Batch learning supports controlled, reproducible retraining on historical data and fits the weekly operating rhythm (d:19, v:19.1).
consequences: Track training data and model versions per run.
Model changes reach production through the release process.

decisions.decision: Write scheduled forecasts to data storage
decisions.context: The system produces weekly forecasts per store and product. The design space describes batch serving that writes predictions to storage, matching this output pattern (d:5).
decisions.rationale: Batch serving can calculate the weekly forecasts and write them to storage for downstream consumers (d:5, v:5.3).
consequences: Define a stable forecast output schema.
Publish each result with its forecast week and model version.

decisions.decision: Keep a previous model version available for rollback
decisions.context: New model ideas should reach production without breaking the weekly run. The design space includes redeploying a previous model version as a rollback option (d:10).

alternatives.label: Rollback to previous model version
pros: Limits disruption from a bad release

decisions.rationale: Retaining a prior model version gives the team a direct recovery path if a new release threatens the weekly forecast run (d:10, v:10.2).
consequences: Retain deployable model artifacts and metadata.
Document and periodically exercise rollback steps.

decisions.decision: Automatically build, test, and deploy models and system components
decisions.context: The team needs a quick path for model ideas while preserving the weekly run. The design space distinguishes automating model and system component delivery from automating pipeline components (d:25).

alternatives.label: Build, test, and deploy models to be served and other system components
Build, test, and deploy machine learning pipelines and components needed during pipeline runs
cons: Does not alone release served models

chosen.label: Build, test, and deploy models to be served and other system components

decisions.rationale: Automating model and component release directly serves the goal of getting new model ideas into production quickly (d:25, v:25.1).
consequences: Gate promotion on model and system checks.
Keep release automation separate from the weekly forecast schedule.

decisions.context: The system must protect a recurring production run while accepting new model ideas. Testing trained model quality is an available pipeline test practice (d:26).
decisions.rationale: Quality checks on trained models give the team a basis to reject candidates that could degrade forecasts (d:26, v:26.9). The checked point had no warnings; both the selected point and the rival were unattested, so the design-space check offers no attestation advantage.
consequences: Define forecast quality thresholds outside the design space.
Retain evaluation results with each model version.

decisions.decision: Monitor model performance and prediction records
decisions.context: Protecting the weekly run requires visibility into forecast quality and the predictions that were produced. The design space covers both performance monitoring and logging data and predictions (d:22).

alternatives.label: Monitoring or logging data and predictions

decisions.rationale: Performance monitoring directly helps detect when a new model or production behavior threatens forecast quality (d:22, v:22.1). Logging inputs and predictions may also be useful for reproducibility, but the brief does not specify its retention needs.
consequences: Set alerts against agreed quality and run health thresholds.
Acquire actual demand outcomes for post-run evaluation.

uncovered: Forecast quality metrics, thresholds, and evaluation windows.
Input data schemas, source systems, late-arriving data, and correction policy.
Storage technology, forecast consumers, access control, and retention requirements.
Schedule timing, run failure recovery, and alert ownership.
Model family, feature design, and forecasting horizon.
Data version repository and model artifact format, retention, and linkage details.
